s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive bilateral nasal airway obstruction with highly vascularized mass
salient_findings: Voluminous, pulsatile, highly vascularized mass in both nasal cavities
Hypervascular tumor with anterior skull base extension
Considerable uptake on radioiodine scintigraphy regarding rib and vertebral lesions
key_facts: Woman in her 30s with no relevant medical history
Progressive bilateral nasal airway obstruction
Endoscopic examination found a voluminous, pulsatile, highly vascularized mass in both nasal cavities
CT scan showed a hypervascular tumor in the nasal cavity, on the left thyroid, the fifth rib, and the L4 vertebra
MRI confirmed a hypervascular tumor with anterior skull base extension
Radioiodine scintigraphy found considerable uptake regarding rib and vertebral lesions
Sinonasal tumor had low uptake on radioiodine scintigraphy
Serum thyroglobulin was significantly elevated at 4432 ng/mL
Biopsy results confirmed VTC metastasis in costal and sinonasal tumor biopsies

s4.champion: Papillary thyroid carcinoma with metastasis to sinonasal cavity

raw.champion: Papillary thyroid carcinoma with metastasis to sinonasal cavity
raw.rationale: The combination of a highly vascularized mass in the nasal cavities, elevated serum thyroglobulin, and biopsy results confirming VTC metastasis, along with the presence of metastases in other parts of the body such as the ribs and vertebrae, points towards a thyroid carcinoma. Papillary thyroid carcinoma is the most common type of thyroid cancer and has a high propensity for metastasis, including to unusual sites like the sinonasal cavity.

rejected.label: Follicular thyroid carcinoma with metastasis to sinonasal cavity
rejected.why: While follicular thyroid carcinoma can also metastasize, the presence of highly vascularized and pulsatile masses is more commonly associated with papillary thyroid carcinoma.

rejected.label: Medullary thyroid carcinoma with metastasis to sinonasal cavity
rejected.why: Medullary thyroid carcinoma typically originates from the parafollicular cells and would not elevate serum thyroglobulin levels as significantly as seen in this case.

rejected.label: Hürthle cell carcinoma with metastasis to sinonasal cavity
rejected.why: Hürthle cell carcinoma is a variant of follicular thyroid carcinoma and is less common than papillary thyroid carcinoma, making it a less likely candidate given the clinical presentation.

rejected.label: Anaplastic thyroid carcinoma with metastasis to sinonasal cavity
rejected.why: Anaplastic thyroid carcinoma is highly aggressive but typically presents in older individuals and is less likely to be the cause of the metastatic disease described, given the patient's age and the nature of the metastases.
